reason: Verified by driving master.html?state=ended and reading render-b.js:1473-1494. Rendered text is exactly: "This link has stopped working. / The day was Saturday 3 October 2026. Ask Orla for a new link. / Nothing has been deleted. Only the link stopped working." The pinned fixture clock is TODAY = 2026-07-16 (fixture.js:17) and primaryDate.date = 2026-10-03 (fixture.js:95) - 79 days AHEAD. So the sentence is factually false as photographed: the only screen in the product that asserts something the data contradicts. It is also the artifact contradicting its own reasoning. The comment at render-b.js:1483 refuses to name a cause because "the surface cannot tell the two apart"; a link that cannot tell whether it was revoked or expired equally cannot know the day has passed, yet the very next line asserts it. The publish screen (render-b.js:1379) promises "You can turn the link off at any time. Anyone holding it then sees that it has ended." - so an off-switch thrown in July is an explicitly supported path, and it lands a guest on a screen telling the couple's family the wedding is over. The contradiction the finding claims between the two screens is verbatim: publish names the state "ended", the state itself names it "stopped working", one state with two names, and the product ships the fault-register one on the screen the audience actually reaches. This is a recurrence of a class already paid for in lessons.md ("Self-contradicting counts... every fact on the surface derives from the rendered data through ONE accessor"): the accessor exists - F.countdown(F.toDay()) already returns the three states ahead/today/passed and is used at render-b.js:1305 and :89 - and this one line reaches past it to a hardcoded tense. The third sentence repeating "stopped working" four lines after the headline is real redundancy on a four-line screen. Not refutable as taste, not restating a gate: interaction-check.mjs:777 only asserts the YEAR STRING appears, which is true of both tenses, so no gate proves the tense correct.
sharpenedFix: Body branches through the accessor already in the file rather than a new date call: var said = F.countdown(F.toDay()); when said.state !== "passed" render "The day is " + F.fmt.longYear(F.project.primaryDate.date) + ". Ask " + F.workspace.owner + " for a new link."; when "passed", keep "The day was ". Headline becomes "This link has ended." - the exact word publish already used, equally cause-neutral (true of revoked and expired alike, which is the whole reason the current wording was chosen) but naming a state rather than a malfunction. Third line becomes "Nothing has been deleted." full stop; the second clause exists only to walk back an alarm the new headline never raises. Note the cost so it is not discovered late: interaction-check.mjs:772, 777 and 780 assert /stopped working/i in the body and in the h1 and must move with the copy - retarget them to /has ended/i and add an assertion that the tense tracks the clock (that the ended body contains "The day is" while F.toDay() > 0), which is the assertion that would have caught this.
